Reference implementation (Python 3.12+):
```python
import random

def randomized_select(values, k, seed=0):
    """Return zero-based kth smallest, expected O(n), worst-case O(n^2)."""
    if not 0<=k<len(values): raise IndexError(k)
    a=list(values); rng=random.Random(seed); lo=0; hi=len(a)-1
    while lo<=hi:
        pivot=a[rng.randrange(lo,hi+1)]; lt=lo; i=lo; gt=hi
        while i<=gt:
            if a[i]<pivot: a[lt],a[i]=a[i],a[lt]; lt+=1; i+=1
            elif a[i]>pivot: a[i],a[gt]=a[gt],a[i]; gt-=1
            else: i+=1
        if k<lt: hi=lt-1
        elif k>gt: lo=gt+1
        else: return a[k]

def deterministic_sort_select(values,k):
    if not 0<=k<len(values): raise IndexError(k)
    return sorted(values)[k]

assert randomized_select([7,2,9,2],1)==deterministic_sort_select([7,2,9,2],1)==2
```
explanation: The randomized 3-way quickselect handles duplicates and has expected O(n) but worst-case O(n²) time; deterministic sorting is O(n log n). Fixed seed makes this comparison repeatable.
